lines.text: # comprehende-182: Agent tooling: Pages publish waits for its deploy, plus check:changed and worktree setup
PR #182. No ticket, one conversation comment. Three independent tooling fixes from one retro, plus AGENTS.md pointer updates.
- Why: present. The PR body says a retro of 10 agent sessions found agents losing time on these tooling gaps.

- Parts: three or four. The Pages deploy wait, `check:changed`, and the worktree setup change could each have been its own PR. The AGENTS.md pointer updates can be a fourth part or sit with the story each hunk serves.
1. Pages publish waits for its deploy: `scripts/pages-review.ts`, `scripts/pages-review.test.ts`, `.agents/skills/pages/SKILL.md`.
4. AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md pointers, alone or with the stories they name.
- `scripts/pages-review.ts publish` now waits for the Pages deploy run of the pushed `gh-pages` commit, reruns it once when it fails, and `--no-wait` skips the wait.
- `pnpm check:changed` runs `vp check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern` on files changed against the merge-base with `origin/main`, plus untracked files.
- Without `T3CODE_PROJECT_ROOT`, `scripts/setup-worktree.ts` links `.env` from the main checkout, the first `git worktree list` entry.
- The Pages wait, `check:changed`, and the worktree setup change are separate parts, each with its own `parts[]` entry.
- `check:changed` passes extra flags such as `--fix` through to `vp check`.
- Do not put the three tooling changes in one part.
- Do not add a `dependsOn` across the three tooling stories.
- This case checks that three fixes from one retro become separate parts, even though one PR body motivates them all.
# vitadeck-150: Stop agents rediscovering how to drive the host window, and fix four repo traps

PR #150. No ticket, no comments. One retro motivates the PR, but the fixes are independent: a GUI drive script, a Docker smoke ownership fix, a shared demo section count, a Pages republish fix, a single stb_ds implementation unit, and docs moves.
- Title: the PR title, or a close paraphrase.
- Why: present. The PR body says a retro of 10 agent sessions found the time goes on stale or missing know-how.
- Size: small to large. Most of the diff is docs and small script fixes; the new 160-line drive script adds the most.
- Parts: about 5. Each fix could have been its own PR. The retro is one motive, not one story.
2. Docker smoke hands back JS output: `scripts/smoke-docker.sh`.
3. One demo section count: `tests/demo_sections.h`, the `DEMO_SECTION_COUNT` hunks of `tests/deck_app_input_harness.c` and `tests/smoke_harness.c`, and the comment in `js/examples/demo/src/App.tsx`.
5. stb_ds compiles once: `src/core/stb_ds.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `src/main.c`, and the removed `STB_DS_IMPLEMENTATION` lines in the harnesses.
6. Agent docs: `AGENTS.md`, `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `docs/releasing.md`, and the build, emulator, and smoke skills.
- `tests/demo_sections.h` defines `DEMO_SECTION_COUNT`; `deck_app_input_harness.c` sets `ROUNDS` from it, and `smoke_harness.c` static-asserts that `PAGES` has one entry per demo section.
- `src/core/stb_ds.c` now holds the only `STB_DS_IMPLEMENTATION`, compiled in `vitadeck_core`; `main.c` and the harnesses drop their own copy.
- `scripts/smoke-docker.sh` now hands back `js/packages/*/dist` and `js/examples/*/.vitadeck` from an EXIT trap, so it also runs when a step fails.
- The fixes are separate parts with their own `parts[]` entries; the shared retro does not make them one story.
- The review rules move from `AGENTS.md` into `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, and `AGENTS.md` keeps a pointer.
- Do not put the whole PR in one part because one retro motivates it.
- Do not put the stb_ds change in the demo section count group, although both touch the same harness files.
- This case checks that independent fixes under one motive become separate parts. `tests/deck_app_input_harness.c` and `tests/smoke_harness.c` hold hunks of two stories, so they have no expect.
# cigster-144: Cloud agent environment fixes from the retro

PR #144. No ticket, no comments. One retro over 14 cloud-agent runs motivates four independent items: a stricter golden threshold with the paint fixes it exposed, an approval policy document, a CI workflow that builds the cloud agent image, and agent steering docs.
- Why: present. The PR body says it implements items from a retro over the last 14 cloud-agent runs.
- Size: medium to very-large. Most files are regenerated golden PNGs.
- Parts: three to five. The golden threshold work, `APPROVAL_POLICY.md`, the image workflow, and the steering docs could each have been its own PR.
- Groups: 4 to 8. The regenerated goldens are a trailing mechanical group of the golden part.
1. Stricter goldens: `e2e/playwright.config.ts`, `e2e/expect.ts`, the seed and visual spec edits, and the paint fixes they exposed.
2. Regenerated goldens: `e2e/snapshots/linux/*.png`, mechanical, last in the golden part.
- The golden threshold drops from `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01` to `0.0003`, and the PR regenerates the goldens.
- A new `Cloud Agent image` workflow builds `.cursor/Dockerfile` when the Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, `daemon.json`, or `environment.json` changes.
- `APPROVAL_POLICY.md` is a new standalone policy document.
- The golden work, the approval policy, and the image workflow are separate parts with their own `parts[]` entries.
- `.oxlintrc.json` adds a lint rule against `test.skip`, and `AGENTS.md` drops the lines that lint now enforces.
- Do not put the whole PR in one part because one retro motivates it.
- Do not put the regenerated PNGs in the approval policy or image workflow part.
- This case checks that items under one retro become separate parts.
